description: Independent, hand-written expectations for the dynamic accessibility-checkpoint negative controls. They are checked against the evidence the lab's captureCheckpoint() produces; they are NOT generated from the scanner's output. Each control is a valid page at load except where a defect is present from load, and the defect named in `what` must be observed only after the interaction/state named by the checkpoints.

fieldGuide.fixture.stateDependent: true when the defect does not exist at page load and only appears after the checkpoint steps (or a media state change). A state-dependent fixture must list at least one rule in pageLoadMustNotReport.
fieldGuide.fixture.pageLoadMustNotReport: engine rules that must NOT be reported at the initial (page-load) checkpoint. This is the proof that a page-load-only scan misses the defect. Every entry carries a `why`.
fieldGuide.checkpoint.steps: trusted Playwright input performed in order: {action:click, role?, name?, selector?}, {action:key, key}, {action:waitForSelector, selector, state}, {action:waitForFunction, expression}, {action:emulateMedia, forcedColors}. Waits are explicit conditions, never fixed sleeps.
fieldGuide.expect.findings: a finding matching engine.id and ruleId (or ruleStartsWith) and targetContains must be present; add "absent": true for a rule that must NOT be reported in this state. An empty array means no finding is required in this state: engine noise such as axe incomplete results is tolerated unless it is asserted.
fieldGuide.expect.noFindings: engines that must report nothing at all in this state (used for the valid-controls negative control).
fieldGuide.expect.state: facts read from record.state.application: dialogsOpen, ariaBrokenRefs, ariaBrokenRefsEmpty, expanded, messages, messagesEmpty, formErrors, visibleTextContains, visibleTextNotContains, details.
fieldGuide.expect.focus: record.focus for bodyFocus/focusVisible/dialogsOpen, otherwise an exact match on record.focus.active (tag, selector, name, role, inDialog, id).
fieldGuide.expect.visual: record.evidence.visual: selector, indicatorPresent/indicatorStyle (focus indicator evidence), iconDeclared/iconBackgroundImageNone (CSS background-image icon evidence).
fieldGuide.expect.changes: recorder evidence for the steps leading to this checkpoint: a change whose `where`/`text` contain the given strings and whose `how` is the expected classification. When how is not "silent", no matching change may be classified silent.
fieldGuide.expect.attributes / expect.visibility: read-only page facts asserted after the checkpoint: attribute presence/value, and whether a role/name or selector is visible to Playwright.
fieldGuide.fixture.validControls: selectors of correctly implemented controls; none of them may be the target of an asserted defect finding.
fieldGuide.fixture.dedupe: one defect observed at several checkpoints is one entry in session.session.findings with one observation per checkpoint.
fieldGuide.fixture.manual: checks a person must still do; the automated evidence cannot decide them.

fixtures.what: A dialog that is closed at page load contains an icon button with no accessible name; axe-core's button-name defect exists only while the dialog is open.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: axe-core ignores the closed <dialog> because it is not rendered, so a page-load scan has no button-name violation. HTML_CodeSniffer reads the DOM regardless of rendering and does report the hidden button at load; this control's page-load miss is therefore axe-specific.

manual: Does the icon button need a name that describes its action, not merely any non-empty name? (4.1.2 cannot be judged from a rule pass alone.)
Is the dialog's own name announced when the dialog opens?

fixtures.what: A button keeps its base :focus ring but loses it under :focus-visible, so the focus indicator disappears only for keyboard focus; nothing changes at page load.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: HTML_CodeSniffer ships SC 2.4.7 only as a manual-review prompt, and axe-core has no focus-indicator rule, so no engine finding is expected at page load (the page-load scan is clean). The defect is only visible in computed styles after trusted keyboard input.

manual: A keyboard-only person must confirm the focused control is actually invisible against the page, not only that its computed outline is none (2.4.7).
Pointer focus still shows the ring by design; only keyboard focus loses it. Check both.

fixtures.what: After a clicked button replaces its controlled panel with a new id, the button's aria-controls still names the removed panel, so the live ARIA reference is broken only in the updated state.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: the aria-controls target exists at page load, so axe-core reports no aria-valid-attr-value violation there; it reports one after the panel id disappears.

manual: Is the new panel announced when it replaces the old one? The ARIA evidence says the reference is broken; it cannot say what was spoken.

fixtures.what: Clicking Save writes "Saved" into a plain div with no role, no aria-live and no focus move; the page is clean at load and the change is silent.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: no engine in the profile reports status text that is painted outside a live region (HTML_CodeSniffer 2.5.1 only offers a manual SC 4.1.3 prompt), and at page load there is no status text at all. The recorder, not an engine, is the evidence.

checkpoints.label: After Save (plain div, not a live region)

manual: Would a person using a screen reader learn that the save succeeded? (4.1.3 requires the message to be exposed as a status message, not merely painted.)
Does any other perceivable mechanism (focus move, sound, persistent text) tell a keyboard user the save happened?

fixtures.what: A modal dialog moves focus to its Close button when it opens and closes with Escape/Close without returning focus to the opener, so focus falls back to body.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: focus restoration is a dynamic behaviour that no engine rule checks, and at page load the dialog is closed, so a page-load scan cannot see it.

checkpoints.label: Dialog closed with Escape (focus not restored)

manual: Close the dialog with Escape and with the Close button: did focus return to the opener for a keyboard user?
Is the opener still reachable, or must the keyboard user start tabbing from the top of the page?

fixtures.what: Two links get their icon only from a CSS background-image; in emulated forced-colours mode the first icon's background-image is removed while the second stays declared.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: axe-core has no rule for a CSS background-image icon disappearing under forced colours, and the light page-load scan finds no image-alt because the page has no . The evidence is the computed background-image before and after emulating forced colours.

checkpoints.label: Forced colours: first icon declaration removed
Forced colours: second icon still declared

manual: Does the icon convey meaning that is lost when it disappears? A background image is not exposed to assistive technology, so the link text must still carry the meaning.

Check the rendered screenshots in forced-colours mode; a declaration is not proof either. (The initial light checkpoint also shows axe's color-contrast returning incomplete on a background-image link: the engine cannot compute contrast there, which is noise, not the defect.)

fixtures.what: A menu is correctly display:none at load, but open-then-close leaves it rendered with opacity:0 and position:absolute, so its items stay in the accessibility tree and are still reachable while the button reports aria-expanded=false.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: at page load the menu is genuinely display:none, so nothing is exposed; after close the content is exposed through opacity:0, which axe-core does not treat as hidden (it has no rule for opacity) and does not report.

manual: After closing the menu, can a screen-reader user still reach the menu items? The ARIA/visibility evidence says yes; a real screen reader should confirm what is announced.
Can a keyboard user reach the invisible items with Tab? The evidence records the exposure, not the tab order.

fixtures.what: Submitting an empty required field shows "Enter your name." next to it, but the input gets no aria-invalid, aria-describedby or aria-errormessage and there is no summary link, so the error exists with no programmatic relationship; nothing changes at load.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: no error exists at page load; when the error appears, neither engine reports an error-association failure (verified on this control), which is why the DOM attributes and the recorder evidence are asserted instead of an engine finding.

manual: Can a screen-reader user find the error message from the field, and is the field announced as invalid? (No aria-invalid/aria-describedby/aria-errormessage is present.)
There is no error summary link; if one is added it must reach a focusable error.

fixtures.what: An unnamed button is visible from page load and unchanged by opening a details element and by opening and closing a dialog; the same button-name finding is observed at every checkpoint and must count once.
manual: One unnamed button is one defect: a fix must remove the finding in every state rather than hiding it in one.
The dialog and details controls are valid and must not gain findings when the unnamed button is fixed.

fixtures.what: The valid counterpart: a dialog named with aria-labelledby, a labelled icon button, a status message in role=status, focus restored to the opener on close, and a labelled form. No axe findings, no silent change for the status message.

pageLoadMustNotReport.why: every button on this page is named; a page-load scan must report nothing.
the page's text and controls meet AA contrast; a page-load scan must report nothing.

checkpoints.label: Dialog closed, focus restored to the opener

manual: Nothing to fix here: this control proves the checkpoints do not invent findings or silent changes on valid markup.
The status message is announced because it is inside role=status; confirm with a real screen reader if a claim about announcements is made.
